tests.summary: `pydicom deidentify` is registered as a subcommand and documents its arguments.
A clean study is released: one readable output file per input file, exit status zero.
Patient Name and Patient ID carry the PREFIX-NNNN pseudonym, with the default and a chosen prefix.
A released image is still the same image: SOP class, modality, dimensions and pixel data survive.
Dates are moved rather than removed: the study date is present, valid and not the original.
Sex, age, size and weight are retained for a patient under ninety.
The crosswalk has the documented header and one row per patient mapping to the pseudonyms used.
A clean run prints the summary line with the right counts and exits zero.
DICOM is recognised by content: a file without an extension is released and a non-DICOM file is skipped and counted.
Files in subdirectories of INPUT_DIR are released.
Every released file says Patient Identity Removed YES and records the profile and both options by code.
deidentify is registered alongside the existing subcommands, which still work.
Acquisition attributes the profile does not list survive in every released image.
Direct identifiers at the top level of a file are gone from the release.
Free-text descriptors that carry identifying text are gone from the release.
Identifiers inside sequence items are removed, not only those at the top level.
Overlay comments and overlay data in a repeating group are removed.
Curve data in a repeating group is removed.
A vendor's private block is removed from the release.
A private block inside a sequence item is removed too.
No released file's name contains an original identifier or an original UID.
A patient identifier shaped like a path cannot place a released file outside OUTPUT_DIR.
A crosswalk path directly inside OUTPUT_DIR is refused: the mapping never lands in the release.
A crosswalk path in a subdirectory of OUTPUT_DIR is refused as well.
The crosswalk is readable by its owner only.
Every released file is readable by its owner only.
OUTPUT_DIR and any directory created under it are owner-only.
An existing crosswalk is not replaced.
A patient name that starts a spreadsheet formula is neutralised in the crosswalk.
Other formula-leading characters, in the name and the ID column, are neutralised too.
Every file under INPUT_DIR is byte-identical after the run.
An OUTPUT_DIR inside INPUT_DIR is refused: nothing new appears under the originals.
One study keeps one Study Instance UID and one Frame of Reference UID across files, and no original UID survives.
A structure set's references resolve to the released image it was drawn on.
The file meta information describes the dataset it fronts.
Every released file is a conformant DICOM file that reads back without forcing.
A patient's dates all move by the same amount, so intervals survive.
No original date survives anywhere in the release, including birth dates and date-times.
Every file of one patient carries the same pseudonym, and different patients carry different ones.
A stated age of ninety or more is released as 090Y.
The released dates do not reveal an age above the cap.
The summary line agrees with what is on disk.
A run that refused or failed a file exits non-zero.
A file whose Burned In Annotation is YES is not released.
A secondary capture or screen save identified by Image Type is not released.
A file that cannot be read, sorted first, does not stop the files after it.
The unreadable file is named on standard error.
A secondary capture whose Image Type says nothing is still not released.
An overlay stored in the unused high bits of the pixels does not leave in the pixels.
Two patients from two hospitals who share an identifier are not merged.
Nothing in the release points at an instance the run refused.
